not_a_result: No held-out cache-enabled confirmation has run. The two-trace cached development run is selection evidence only. This protocol does not alter the failed earlier confirmations.
preflight: Require an eligible one-worker preflight no more than 120 seconds old at launch, pinned to CPU 0 inside the exact frozen cgroup budget. This preflight does not guarantee future availability; every confirmation arm independently retains and gates CPU-steal counters.
quality: Every request token IDs, text, prompt length and task-correctness classification must match the primary native baseline, with zero failures. Report absolute strict copy-task accuracy, including incorrect answers and EOS/cap finishes.
uncertainty: 10,000 fixed-seed hierarchical paired bootstrap replicates; sessions then whole paired traces. Require latency and throughput thresholds in every session and corresponding confidence bounds. No optional stopping, added traces or relaxed thresholds.
scope: One backend thread, benchmark/control/native processes pinned to CPU 0 inside a dedicated 0.92 CPU cgroup. Same Qwen2.5-0.5B FP16, tokenizer, greedy sampler, output limits and context. Native latency and throughput development leaders both qualify as challengers. No broad engine/model-quality, production, GPU or 1.0 claim.
failure_policy: Retain and report every result and gate failure. New prompts/framing/cache settings do not repair previous failed confirmations. Any CPU, cache-path, quality, performance or resource gate failure invalidates qualification; do not drop or selectively rerun traces.
